title: Elbridge Colby Responds to Mearsheimer on China at All-In Summit
summary: A US defence strategist agrees China seeks regional hegemony, argues for denial with Asian allies over nuclear risk, and warns the US and Taiwan are under-investing to defend Taiwan.

assertions.quote: I agree that that China has rational incentives for regional hegemony it's standard behav

verdicts.note: CSIS quotes the 2022 US National Security Strategy: Beijing 'has ambitions to create an enhanced sphere of influence in the Indo-Pacific and to become the world's leading power'.
DDIS: China seeks to establish itself as the dominant power in Asia and a leading global great power, pressuring neighbours politically, economically and militarily.
US intelligence says China aims to dominate its region and challenge Washington's leadership.
The Munich Security Report says an ever more powerful China is making a forceful bid for regional dominance.

assertions.quote: rather to have a military that works with those militaries that I talked about like Japan India

verdicts.note: CSIS concludes that 'a successful defense is possible, and deterrence is achievable' if China doubts it can prevail; it argues the deterrence logic but did not test it.

assertions.quote: the stopping power of water which is a pretty in it's like it's hard to invade other people across water

verdicts.note: DoD: an amphibious invasion would be 'one of the most complicated and difficult military operations for the PLA', needing air and maritime superiority and a rapid build-up and sustainment of forces, at enormous risk to China.
CSIS: 'It is harder to cross 160 km of water than to cross a land border', and once a landing has begun there is no going back, a much greater challenge than Russia faced in Ukraine.
US intelligence says Chinese officials themselves recognise that an amphibious invasion of Taiwan would be extremely challenging.

assertions.quote: we have not prioritized Asia and the Taiwanese are laggardly

verdicts.note: Taiwan's defence spending stayed near 2.5% of GDP and US forces were pulled to other theatres, though both have since pledged increases.
CSIS finds severe weaknesses in Taiwan's ground forces and says it must fill its ranks and train, but this is a judgment about priorities rather than a measure of whether total investment deters.

verdicts.note: Front lines moved little through 2023 and 2024 while both sides traded heavy losses of men and materiel.

verdicts.note: Some great powers have fought for economic spheres, as Japan did in 1941, but since 1945 most have sought economic influence through trade and investment rather than conquest.

In the case file, England's 17th-century wars with the Dutch were fought for trade ('What we want is more of the trade the Dutch now have'), and a commercial rivalry escalated into a strategic one and then war. These are historical cases only.
